Before The Court Of I Addl. Small Causes Judge & Acjm &

 Present: Sri.Narendra.B.R., B.Sc, L.L.B.

 1. HDFC ERGO General Insurance  Insurance Company Ltd.,
 No.25/1, 2nd Floor,
 Shankarayana Building,

 Bengaluru - 560001. 
 (Insurer of vehicle bearing  Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542). 
 (Policy No.2315204846059500000 Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
1  Valid from 20.08.2022 to 19.08.2023).
 2. Sri.Sangappa,
 S/o.Malappa Gujamangadi,
 Aged about 28 years,
 R/at No.122, Bijagal Village,

 (RC Owner of vehicle bearing  Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542).
 (R1 - By Sri.V.R.Muralidhara, Adv.)
 (R2 - By Smt.Dhanalakshmi, Adv.)
 J U D G M E N T This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him. 
2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 13.02.2023 at about 12.45 p.m., when the petitioner was proceeding on Bike bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JG-2186, as a pillion rider, from 8th mile side towards the Nelagndaranahalli, near Nagasandra Circle, a Canter Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's bike. Due to said accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Thereafter he was shifted to Sarojini Health Center Hospital, Bengaluru and later shifted to People Tree Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .6,50,000/-
towards medical, food, nourishment, conveyance and other incidental expenses. 
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing the work of Head Cook and also an agriculturist and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries,
he has suffered permanent disability. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter by its driver. The respondents, being insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. 
3. On service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through their counsel and filed their written statement. Though respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel,
he has not filed the written statement. 
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 specifically denied the contents of claim petition. 
The respondent No.1 denied the age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident, involvement of offending vehicle and injuries sustained by the petitioner. The respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed. Respondent No.1 admitted the issue of Goods Carrying Comprehensive Policy bearing No.2315204846059500000 in favour of second respondent in respect of Goods vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 and the liability, if any, is subject to the Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
2 terms and conditions of policy. Further contended that second respondent willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license, permit and fitness certificate to drive the same as on the date of accident. Further contended that the rider of motor cycle riding his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and attributed more negligence for causing the alleged accident and there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of insured vehicle. Further the rider of motor cycle was riding his vehicle without wearing safety headgear and without having DL and insurance to his vehicle at the time of accident. The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant. Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition. 
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 13.02.2023 at about 12.45 p.m., near Nagasandra Circle,
Nelagadaranahalli Main Road, Rukmaninagar, Nagasandra, Bengaluru, when he was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JG-2186 as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 by its driver? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award? 
6. In order to prove the contents of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and Dr.Ramesh B, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 documents and closed his side of evidence. The respondents not adduced their evidence either oral or documentary. 
7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8. Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 13.02.2023 at about 12.45 p.m., near Nagasandra Circle, Nelagadaranahalli Main Road, Rukmaninagar, Nagasandra, Bengaluru, when he was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-02-JG-2186, as a pillion rider, due to the rash Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
3 and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 by its driver accident was caused due to which he sustained grievous injuries. 
10. In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of canter, the petitioner produced Ex.P1 & 2 - FIR and First Information is lodged by the petitioner himself police on 14.02.2023. On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC. After registration police went near the place of accident and drew spot panchanama & sketch as per Ex.P.3 by narrating the place of accident. The FIR is registered against the driver of canter alleging that the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving. In first information statement also, it is alleged that the accident took place due rash and negligence on the part of driver of canter. After registration of FIR, the police conducted the investigation by visiting the place of incident which aspect could be noticed as per Ex.P.3. As per the sketch, the petitioner appears to have riding the motorcycle in the left and the offending vehicle appears to have been driven from right side towards the left where the vehicle of petitioner was proceeding. The sketch depicts the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of canter, as contended by petitioner. The respondent No.1 contended that the accident took place due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle. The jurisdictional police appears to have conducted the investigation and filed the final report against the driver of canter, as per Ex.P.6, for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act. In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of canter vehicle. The police conducted detailed investigation and filed final report against the driver of canter vehicle alleging negligence on his part in the cause of accident. The respondent No.1 denied the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of canter and contended that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle. The respondent No.1 not furnished any materials in order to substantiate their contention. The allegations made in FIR and final report does not appear to have been challenged, either by driver or owner of the canter, in any manner. In the FIR as well as final report,
the cause of accident is stated to be rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver. Respondent No.1 not placed any materials to rebut or contradict the documents furnished on behalf of petitioner. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials to prove that there is no negligence on the part of driver of canter. If there is negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle, then final report could not have been filed against the driver of canter. No materials are placed to rebut or controvert the said documents or the recitals mentioned therein. In the absence of satisfactory materials, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be relied for ascertaining the aspect of negligence. The documents furnished by petitioners substantiate their contention pertaining to negligence on the part of driver of canter. 
11. Further, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1. In his chief examination he deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver, the accident occurred. PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination, nothing to disprove the contention of petitioner could be elicited. Nothing to dispute the rash or negligence of driver of canter could be elicited in the cross examination of PW.1. Nothing to disprove or doubt the documents furnished by petitioner, related to negligence of canter driver, could be elicited during the cross examination of PW.1. On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing is elicited from PW.1 to disprove the case of petitioner. 
Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
4 12. The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner. On perusal of entire record, the accident appears to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of canter. Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P6, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner. Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative. 
13. Issue No.2: In view of held issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation. In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment. In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced the Wound certificate issued by Akash Hospital marked at Ex.P.5, wherein it is mentioned that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature. On perusal of records, the petitioner appears to have took treatment in hospital as an inpatient as per Ex.P7, Discharge Summary issued by People Tree Hospitals. The petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh.B as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P11 & 12 documents. PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability of right lower limb to the extent of 24% and to the whole body at 12%. By considering the nature of injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering. 
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses: The petitioner claimed compensation towards medical expenses. 
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital. The petitioner produced 29 Medical bills amounting to .59,559/- as per Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10 - Final bill for a sum of Rs.3,70,000/-. The bills produced by petitioner totally amounts to Rs.4,29,559/-. 
The respondents not furnished any cogent and satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to medical expenses incurred by him. In the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worth to disprove those bills could be elicited. It is suggested to PW.1 that the bills furnished are created for availing compensation which is denied by the witness. The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent and satisfactory materials. On consideration of the materials on record, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .4,29,559/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses. 
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges: On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 13.02.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital. 
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital due to the injuries sustained by him. During the time of treatment, the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment. The petitioner produced Ex.P.7 - Discharge Summary issued by People Tree Hospitals, wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner taken treatment as an inpatient from Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
5 13.02.2023 to 27.02.2023 i.e., for a period of 15 days. Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 15 days amounting to a sum of .7,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant. 
(iv) Towards Conveyance: 
The petitioner is the resident of Raghavendra Nagar, Omkar Nagar, Andrahalli Village, Bengaluru, and he got admitted to the hospital for availing treatment. In order to prove said aspect, the petitioner produced Discharge Summary marked at Ex.P.7. Considering the injuries and facts of the case , the tribunal is of view that compensation of .10,000/- appear just and proper towards conveyance charges. 
(v) Towards loss of income during treatment: The petitioner contended that he was working as Head Cook and also doing agriculture and earning a sum of .25,000/-
per month. In order to prove his income, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that he was earning .25,000/- per month. The petitioner has not furnished any materials to prove his contentions pertaining to occupation and income. 
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income is to be taken into consideration. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-. On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .32,000/- towards loss of income during treatment. 
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity: 
The petitioner contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement. The petitioner got examined Dr.Ramesh B, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2. PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess the disabilities. The doctor deposed that petitioner sustained major crush injury with circumferential deploying of skin and subcutaneous right leg fibula head undisplaced fracture and he underwent wound debridement and physics grafting and later discharged. The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to right lower limb to the extent of 24% and to the whole body at 12%. In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.11 & 12 i.e., OPD Record and X-ray film. In the evidence, PW.2 deposed that the petitioner is not able sit with crossed legs and unable to stand for long time on the affected limb. Though PW.2 stated about the said difficulties, he has not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do any work at all. The witness also not stated about the actual impact caused to the work of petitioner due to the injuries sustained. 
Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
6 By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty. As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%. 
In order to prove age of the petitioner, he has produced Ex.P.8 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1975. The accident occurred on 13.02.2023. Except Aadhar card, the petitioner not furnished any materials to prove his age. The respondents not furnished any materials to rebut or disprove the entries in the Aadhar card related to age of petitioner and not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to disprove the age of petitioner. As per the document furnished by petitioner, his age is 48 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier. As per the ratio laid in Smt.Sarla Verma case the applicable multiplier is '13'. As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income. Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (10% of prior annual income) = .19,200/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 13 Loss of future earnings - (.19,200/- x 13) = .2,49,600/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .2,49,600/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier. The doctor, who examined the petitioner, not stated that the petitioner is unable to do his daily work. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities. 
14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
 Sl . No . Particulars Amount  a. Towards injury pain and .50,000/-
 suffering  b. Towards Medical Expenses .4,29,559/-
 c. Towards food and extra .7,500/-
 nourishment and medical  attendant Shivananjegowda vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 28 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126342402/
7  d. Towards conveyance .10,000/-
 e. Towards loss of income .32,000/-
 during treatment  f. Towards loss of future .2,49,600/-
 earning  g. Deprivation of future .10,000/-
 amenities  Total compensation .7,88,659/-
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of .7,88,659/-.
15. In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law. Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908. Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded." 
In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2. It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing Regn.No.KA-37-A-8542 by its driver. So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative. 
17. Issue No.3: In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost. 
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .7,88,659/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Eighty Eight Thousand Six Hundred and Fifty Nine only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

8 Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner. Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award. 
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019. 
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court. The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-. Draw up award accordingly.
